```{r setup}
source("_data.R")
# Public-safe by construction: this page only shows the 36 labelled (public) hostnames and aggregates.
# Dark surface #0f1512; group colours are the ones validated for it in decision-models.qmd (dataviz validator, all pairs, dark).
group_cols <- c("ad exchange" = "#d95926", "tracker" = "#3987e5", "legitimate" = "#199e70")
theme_story <- function() theme_minimal(base_size = 12, base_family = "sans") + theme(
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#0f1512", colour = NA), panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#0f1512", colour = NA),
  text = element_text(colour = "#e2e9e4"), axis.text = element_text(colour = "#93a39a"),
  panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none", plot.margin = margin(4, 8, 4, 4))

abbr <- c(advertising = "ad", tracking = "tracking", telemetry = "telemetry", malicious = "malware",
          content = "content", service = "service", unknown = "?")
OA <- "gpt-6-luna"   # the model behind OpenAI's Decisions API; the story calls it the Decisions API
col_order <- intersect(c(OA, "Jev", "Strands 2B", "Strands E4B", "Sonnet"), models_all)
col_labels <- c(`gpt-6-luna` = "Decisions API", `Jev` = "Jev", `Strands 2B` = "Strands 2B", `Strands E4B` = "Strands E4B", `Sonnet` = "Sonnet")
tiles <- lab_all
tiles$cls <- ifelse(tiles$category %in% BLOCK, "block", ifelse(tiles$category == "unknown", "unknown", "other"))
tiles$txt <- abbr[tiles$category]
top3 <- intersect(c(OA, "Jev", "Sonnet"), models_all)
strands <- c("Strands 2B", "Strands E4B")

# One grid per group, so a sticky fits one screen. Highlight = colour: inside the focus, a blocking answer takes the
# group's colour (what the host is); everything outside the focus stays readable in greys.
tile_plot <- function(g, focus_models = models_all, focus_hosts = NULL) {
  d <- tiles[tiles$group == g, ]
  d$hostname <- factor(d$hostname, levels = rev(sort(unique(d$hostname))))
  d$model <- factor(as.character(d$model), levels = col_order)
  on <- d$model %in% focus_models & (is.null(focus_hosts) | d$hostname %in% focus_hosts)
  d$key <- paste(d$cls, ifelse(on, "on", "off"))
  fills <- c(`block on` = group_cols[[g]], `other on` = "#2a3631", `unknown on` = "#0f1512",
             `block off` = "#3a4741", `other off` = "#19221e", `unknown off` = "#0f1512")
  inks <- c(`block on` = "#ffffff", `other on` = "#e2e9e4", `unknown on` = "#e2e9e4",
            `block off` = "#b9c4be", `other off` = "#5f6d66", `unknown off` = "#4a5550")
  ggplot(d, aes(model, hostname)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = key), colour = "#0f1512", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = txt, colour = key), size = 3.3, family = "sans", fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fills) + scale_colour_manual(values = inks) +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top", labels = col_labels) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_story() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#e2e9e4"))
}
cat_n <- function(m, g) { d <- tiles[tiles$model == m & tiles$group == g, ]; sum(d$cls == "block") }
n_g <- function(g) sum(hosts$group == g)
ag <- "ad exchange"; tg <- "tracker"; lg <- "legitimate"
jev_missed <- tiles$hostname[tiles$group == ag & tiles$model == "Jev" & tiles$cls != "block"]
oa_missed <- tiles$hostname[tiles$group == ag & tiles$model == OA & tiles$cls != "block"]
legit_flags <- sum(tiles$group == lg & tiles$cls == "block")
oa_in <- mstat(OA, "tokens_in_total"); oa_n <- mstat(OA, "n")   # every host asked, household included (totals only)
oa_s <- mstat(OA, "ms_median") / 1000
code <- function(x) paste(sprintf("<code>%s</code>", x), collapse = " and ")
```

```{=html}
<header class="story-hero">
  <p class="kicker">Decision models</p>
  <h1>OpenAI’s Decisions API, put to a household test</h1>
  <p class="dek">OpenAI’s new API answers with typed judgements a program can act on, not with chat. One home network asked it which unfamiliar hostnames are ads, alongside TypeSafe’s Jev, two open models that run on your own computer, and a chatbot.</p>
  <p class="byline">October 2026 · tests run on 18 October</p>
</header>
```

::: {.story-body}

::: {.lede}
This month OpenAI opened its Decisions API to developers as a public beta. The model behind it, gpt-6-luna, does not write text. You send it a piece of evidence and typed questions, and it sends back probabilities and a confidence that a program can branch on. It has been billed as OpenAI's answer to TypeSafe's Jev, the model that made this kind of "decision model" a product.
:::

That made it worth trying on a real problem. On 4 October an ad slipped into an iPhone app on a home network, even though every device there filters its lookups through Pi-hole, a small DNS ad blocker. Pi-hole only blocks hostnames that are already on its blocklists; anything new goes straight through. Jev already runs a weekly check of that household's unfamiliar hostnames. Could the Decisions API do the job as well?

Each hostname got the same three questions: *which of seven categories fits? how unwanted is it, from 0 to 4? is it run by an ad-tech company?* The test set was `r nrow(hosts)` hostnames labelled by hand: `r n_g(ag)` ad exchanges, `r n_g(tg)` trackers and `r n_g(lg)` ordinary sites. Jev and two open Strands models answered the same questions, and Anthropic's Sonnet, a general chatbot, got them in plain English as a reference point. None of them could look anything up; each answered from what it already knew.

:::

:::{.cr-section}

Start with the `r n_g(ag)` <span class="key ad">ad exchanges</span>: companies whose whole business is serving and auctioning ads. Each row is a hostname, each column a model. **A coloured tile means the model put it in a blocking category**: advertising, tracking or malware. @cr-ads

The Decisions API named a blocking category for `r if (cat_n(OA, ag) == n_g(ag)) sprintf("all %d", n_g(ag)) else sprintf("%d of %d", cat_n(OA, ag), n_g(ag))`. @cr-ads-oa

Jev, the household's current check, got `r cat_n("Jev", ag)`, and Sonnet `r cat_n("Sonnet", ag)`. @cr-ads-top

The two Strands models are small enough to run on an ordinary computer with no internet connection. They mostly shrugged: a "?" means they answered *unknown*. The 2B model caught `r cat_n("Strands 2B", ag)` and E4B `r cat_n("Strands E4B", ag)`. @cr-ads-strands

`r if (length(jev_missed) && !length(intersect(jev_missed, oa_missed))) sprintf("The one ad exchange Jev let through, %s, the Decisions API caught.", code(jev_missed)) else if (length(oa_missed)) sprintf("The Decisions API let through %s.", code(oa_missed)) else "Neither the Decisions API nor Jev missed any."` @cr-ads-miss

<span class="key tracker">Trackers</span> are a harder case: they are mostly analytics companies rather than ad sellers. `r trk <- sapply(top3, \(m) cat_n(m, tg)); if (length(unique(trk)) == 1) sprintf("The Decisions API, Jev and Sonnet each called all %d of them", n_g(tg)) else sprintf("The Decisions API called %d of the %d, Jev %d and Sonnet %d", trk[OA], n_g(tg), trk["Jev"], trk["Sonnet"])` a tracker or an ad host; the Strands models managed `r cat_n("Strands 2B", tg)` and `r cat_n("Strands E4B", tg)`. @cr-trk

For a household, the result that matters most is this one. A wrong block breaks a website, and **`r if (legit_flags == 0) "none of the five models" else sprintf("%d answers", legit_flags)` put any of the `r n_g(lg)`** <span class="key legit">ordinary sites</span> **in a blocking category.** @cr-legit

stat <- function(n, l) cat(sprintf('<div class="stat"><div class="num">%s</div><div class="lab">%s</div></div>\n', n, l))
caught <- sapply(models_all, \(m) sum(tiles$model == m & tiles$cls == "block" & tiles$group != lg))
also <- setdiff(names(caught)[caught == caught[OA]], OA)
stat(sprintf("%d of %d", caught[OA], sum(hosts$unwanted_host)), sprintf("ad and tracker hosts the Decisions API put in a blocking category%s", if (length(also)) sprintf(" (%s matched it)", paste(also, collapse = " and ")) else ""))
stat(as.character(sum(tiles$model == OA & tiles$group == lg & tiles$cls == "block")), "ordinary sites it wrongly put in a blocking category")
stat(sprintf("$%.2f", oa_in * 0.10 / 1e6), sprintf("what the Decisions API cost for all %d hostnames tested", oa_n))
stat(sprintf("%.1f s", oa_s), "its time per hostname, two requests over the network")

alone_all <- H$flagged_by[["0"]]

## How sure is it?

A decision model doesn't just pick an answer; it says how sure it is. A program can use that to act on the easy cases and send the hard ones to a person. Each model was also asked the category question twice, with the options in reverse order, because a model that leans towards the first option listed will change its answer.

:::{.cr-section}

Each dot is one hostname: all `r n_c[[OA]]` that were tested, including the household's own. The further right, the surer the model was of its category. @cr-conf-all

The Decisions API was often sure, though less often than Jev: median confidence `r sprintf("%.2f", med_c[OA])`, with `r hi_c[OA]` of `r n_c[OA]` hostnames at 0.85 or above. Jev was surer (median `r sprintf("%.2f", med_c["Jev"])`, `r hi_c["Jev"]` above 0.85). Reversing the options changed the Decisions API's category for `r flips[OA]` hostnames and Jev's for `r flips["Jev"]`. @cr-conf-top

The Strands models were almost never sure (medians `r sprintf("%.2f", med_c["Strands 2B"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", med_c["Strands E4B"])`). A model that is unsure of everything gives a program nothing to act on: every hostname would go to a person. @cr-conf-strands

## From answers to decisions

The household's weekly check doesn't block on the category alone. It proposes a block only when both option orders agree on a blocking category, with confidence of at least 0.85, **and** one of the other two questions agrees: an unwanted score of 2.5 or more, or an ad-tech answer of 0.5 or more. Anything doubtful goes to a person. The rule never unblocks anything.

:::{.cr-section}

Here are the unwanted scores, by model. <span class="key ad">Ad exchanges</span> sit near 3, *ad serving or tracking*, and <span class="key legit">ordinary sites</span> near 1. @cr-score-all

The <span class="key tracker">trackers</span> sit near 2, which is the scale's own level for *third-party analytics*. The Decisions API put them at a median of `r sprintf("%.1f", trk_score[OA])`, below the 2.5 line. @cr-score-trk

The ad-tech question doesn't rescue them either. The Decisions API reads it literally: analytics companies aren't ad-tech, so it put only `r trk_adtech[OA]` of the `r n_g(tg)` trackers over 0.5. Jev put `r trk_adtech["Jev"]`. @cr-adtech-trk

So under this rule the Decisions API blocks `r vb(OA)` of the `r sum(hosts$unwanted_host)` unwanted hostnames automatically and sends `r vr(OA)` to a person, missing `r vm(OA)`. Jev blocks `r vb("Jev")`, sends `r vr("Jev")` and misses `r vm("Jev")`. Neither proposed blocking an ordinary site. The rule's cut-offs were set for Jev, which is part of why it comes out ahead here. @cr-rule

:::

```{r cost-cards, results='asis'}
card <- function(name, lead, rows) cat(sprintf('<div class="card%s"><h3>%s</h3><dl>%s</dl></div>\n', if (lead) " lead" else "", name,
  paste(sprintf("<dt>%s</dt><dd>%s</dd>", names(rows), rows), collapse = "")))
card("OpenAI Decisions API", TRUE, c(Time = sprintf("%.2f s per hostname", ms_med(OA)), Cost = sprintf("$%.3f for %d hostnames", oa_in * 0.10 / 1e6, oa_n), Sees = "hostnames only"))
card("Jev", FALSE, c(Time = sprintf("%.2f s (%d timed)", ms_med("Jev"), ms_n("Jev")), Cost = "no published price", Sees = "hostnames only"))
card("Strands 2B", FALSE, c(Time = sprintf("%.2f s on a Mac", ms_med("Strands 2B")), Cost = "free", Sees = "nothing leaves the computer"))
card("Strands E4B", FALSE, c(Time = sprintf("%.2f s on a Mac", ms_med("Strands E4B")), Cost = "free", Sees = "nothing leaves the computer"))
if (have_son) card("Sonnet", FALSE, c(Time = sprintf("%.1f s, one prompt", median(son$latency_s)), Cost = "not priced here", Sees = "hostnames only"))
```

```{=html}
</div>
```

::: {.story-body}

Times are for two requests per hostname (forward and reversed options), except Sonnet's single prompt. The cloud models' times include the network. No service was ever sent a device name or an address, only the hostname.

## Was it a fair test?

Mostly, with limits worth knowing.

- **Same inputs.** Every model saw only the hostname and the same questions. None could search the web: Sonnet's replies record `r son_tool_uses` tool uses across all `r son_replies`.
- **The rule was built for Jev.** The 0.85 and 2.5 cut-offs were set for Jev, before the Decisions API was tested, so the decision-rule results favour Jev. The raw answers in the first section don't use any rule.
- **Few, famous hostnames.** Thirty-six hand-labelled hostnames, mostly well-known ad companies, is a demonstration, not a benchmark. One or two hostnames either way is noise, and there are no truly hard cases.
- **Sonnet had a different prompt.** It got category names without descriptions, was asked once, and wrote its numbers as text. It's a reference point, not a contestant.
- **One run each, on different days.** Sonnet answered on 4 October and the decision models mostly on 18 October (some of Jev's answers date from 4 October). Nobody measured how much each model's answers vary from run to run.

## What it means

On this test the Decisions API did what it promises. It recognised every ad and tracker host with no false alarms, it was confident often enough for a program to act on, and at `r sprintf("$%.2f", oa_in * 0.10 / 1e6)` for `r oa_n` hostnames it is cheap. It is also the only model here with a published price.

Its one quirk is that it reads questions literally. Asked whether an analytics company is ad-tech, it says no. Under a rule tuned for Jev, that means fewer automatic blocks and more for a person to review, not more mistakes. Jev stays the household's weekly check for now, and the Decisions API is a strong second opinion. The small Strands models aren't ready for this job yet.

:::

<p class="note">Sources: the test results saved on 4 and 18 October 2026. The Decisions API is in public beta, and gpt-6-luna may change before general release. Only the 36 public test hostnames and totals appear on this page.</p>
